title: First homework, then play: a first-then board
group: LDS-FOCUS — Focus and Getting Things Done
examples: How do I make myself do homework?
I want to play, not do homework

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: Sometimes you want to play before homework. Lots of people feel that way. Look at the board. It has two boxes. One says first, and one says then. This is a first-then board.

draw.text: First homework, then play: a first-then board

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: Look at the pencil in the first box. First, homework. You do the work one small bit at a time. You only think about this box now. Can you say it with me? First, homework.

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: Now look at the ball in the then box. Then, play. This is the fun part, and it comes next. Knowing play comes next can help you keep going. What fun thing would you put in your then box?

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: When you feel stuck, look back at the first box. You can say, First homework, then play. If the work is too hard, ask for help. You can say, Can you help me, please? Asking for help is a good choice.

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: The homework is done, so now you can play. Well done. Today, make a first-then card for one more job. For example, first brush teeth, then story time.

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

faq.a: It is a card with two boxes. The first box shows the job to do now. The then box shows the fun thing that comes after.
Something you enjoy, like playing outside, drawing, building blocks or a story. Choose it with a grown-up before you start.
asks: What goes in the then box?

faq.q: What if my homework is too hard?
faq.a: Do one small part, then stop and ask. You can say, Can you help me, please? A grown-up you trust can help.

faq.q: What if I really do not want to start?
faq.a: Look only at the first box. Do just one question. Starting is the hardest bit, and then it gets easier.
asks: I do not want to do it

faq.q: Can I use first-then for other things?
faq.a: Yes. First bath, then story. First shoes, then park. It works for any job that feels tricky.
asks: Where else can I use it?

facts: A first-then board has exactly two boxes: the job now and the reward next.
Many teachers use first-then boards to help children know what is coming.

quiz.say: Look at a first-then board. What goes in the first box?
quiz.show: What goes in the first box?
quiz.why: The first box shows the job you do now. The fun thing comes after it.

wrong.0: The fun thing goes in the then box, after the job.
wrong.2: The first box holds a picture of the job you do now.

quiz.say: Sam's board says first homework, then play. When does Sam play?
quiz.show: First homework, then play. When does Sam play?

options.show: In the middle of his work
options.say: In the middle of his work

quiz.why: Then means after. Sam plays when his homework is finished.

wrong.0: Homework is in the first box, so it comes before play.
wrong.1: Sam finishes all of the homework first, then he plays.
